executive_summary.scope_statement: This assessment evaluates the security posture of the ArchScale multi-tenant platform. It covers authentication surfaces, OAuth configuration, HTTP security headers, SSL/TLS, CORS policies, DNS infrastructure, subdomain enumeration, port scanning, technology fingerprinting, cookie security, Content Security Policy, rate limiting, and error handling.

findings.title: Missing Content-Security-Policy header on Main Application
findings.description: CSP prevents XSS, clickjacking, and other injection attacks
findings.impact: Without Content-Security-Policy, the application is vulnerable to attacks that this header mitigates
findings.remediation: Implement a strict Content-Security-Policy that restricts script-src, style-src, and default-src to trusted origins

findings.title: Missing X-Frame-Options header on Main Application
findings.description: Prevents clickjacking by controlling framing of the page
findings.impact: Without X-Frame-Options, the application is vulnerable to attacks that this header mitigates
findings.remediation: Add header: X-Frame-Options: DENY (or SAMEORIGIN if framing is needed internally)

findings.title: Missing X-Content-Type-Options header on Main Application
findings.description: Prevents MIME-sniffing attacks
findings.impact: Without X-Content-Type-Options, the application is vulnerable to attacks that this header mitigates
findings.remediation: Add header: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff

findings.title: Missing X-XSS-Protection header on Main Application
findings.description: Legacy XSS filter (deprecated but still relevant for older browsers)
findings.impact: Without X-XSS-Protection, the application is vulnerable to attacks that this header mitigates
findings.remediation: Add header: X-XSS-Protection: 0 (rely on CSP instead) or 1; mode=block for legacy support

findings.title: Missing Referrer-Policy header on Main Application
findings.description: Controls how much referrer information is sent with requests
findings.impact: Without Referrer-Policy, the application is vulnerable to attacks that this header mitigates
findings.remediation: Add header: Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin

findings.title: Missing Permissions-Policy header on Main Application
findings.description: Controls which browser features the page can use (camera, mic, geolocation)
findings.impact: Without Permissions-Policy, the application is vulnerable to attacks that this header mitigates
findings.remediation: Add header: Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()

findings.title: Missing X-Permitted-Cross-Domain-Policies header on Main Application
findings.description: Prevents Flash/PDF cross-domain data loading
findings.impact: Without X-Permitted-Cross-Domain-Policies, the application is vulnerable to attacks that this header mitigates
findings.remediation: Add header: X-Permitted-Cross-Domain-Policies: none

findings.title: Information disclosure via Server on Main Application
findings.description: Reveals server software and version — aids attacker reconnaissance
findings.impact: Attackers can use this information to identify specific vulnerabilities in the disclosed software version
findings.remediation: Remove or anonymize the Server header to reduce information disclosure

findings.title: HTTP to HTTPS redirect uses 308 instead of 301 on app.archscale.in
findings.description: HTTP to HTTPS redirect uses status code 308. A 301 (Permanent Redirect) is preferred for SEO and browser caching.
findings.impact: Temporary redirects may not be cached by browsers, causing unnecessary HTTP requests
findings.remediation: Use 301 (Moved Permanently) for HTTP to HTTPS redirects

findings.title: HTTP to HTTPS redirect uses 308 instead of 301 on auth.archscale.in
findings.description: HTTP to HTTPS redirect uses status code 308. A 301 (Permanent Redirect) is preferred for SEO and browser caching.

findings.title: SPF record uses ~all (soft fail — not enforced)
findings.description: The SPF record uses ~all (soft fail). While emails from unauthorized senders will be flagged, they won't be rejected outright.
findings.impact: Spoofed emails may still be delivered to some recipients
findings.remediation: Consider changing ~all to -all for strict enforcement once all legitimate senders are listed

findings.title: DMARC policy is set to 'none' (monitoring only)
findings.description: DMARC policy is set to p=none, which only monitors but does not reject or quarantine spoofed emails.
findings.impact: Email spoofing is monitored but not prevented
findings.remediation: Consider upgrading to p=quarantine or p=reject after reviewing DMARC reports

findings.title: Certificate Transparency reveals 25 subdomains for archscale.in
findings.description: Certificate Transparency logs reveal 25 subdomains for archscale.in. While CT logs are public by design, exposed subdomains increase the attack surface.
findings.evidence: Subdomains found: academy.archscale.in, accounts.archscale.in, admin.archscale.in, ai.archscale.in, api.archscale.in, api.cloud.archscale.in, app.archscale.in, archscale.in, auth.archscale.in, cdn.archscale.in, client.archscale.in, cloud.archscale.in, community.archscale.in, docs.archscale.in, forms.archscale.in...
findings.impact: Each subdomain is a potential attack vector that may host vulnerable services
findings.remediation: Audit all discovered subdomains. Ensure staging/dev/internal subdomains are not publicly accessible.

findings.title: CORS allows all origins (wildcard) on Main Application
findings.description: The server sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin to wildcard (*), allowing any website to make cross-origin requests.
findings.impact: Any website can read responses from this endpoint. If the endpoint returns sensitive data, it can be stolen cross-origin.
findings.remediation: Replace wildcard with specific trusted origins. Use a whitelist-based approach.

findings.title: Technology fingerprint: 3 technologies detected
findings.description: Technology fingerprinting detected 3 technologies across all scanned endpoints.
findings.evidence:
• Cloudflare  (CDN/WAF) — detected in: Main Application (header), Main Application (waf), Login Page (header), Login Page (waf), Auth Service (waf), Auth Service (header)
  • Cloudflare WAF  (WAF/CDN) — detected in: Auth Service (waf), Main Application (waf), Login Page (waf)
  • Vercel  (WAF/CDN) — detected in: Auth Service (waf), Main Application (waf), Login Page (waf)
findings.impact: Technology fingerprint helps attackers identify version-specific vulnerabilities and tailor their attacks
findings.remediation: Remove version information from response headers. Suppress X-Powered-By. Configure Server header to be generic.

findings.title: WAF/CDN detected: Cloudflare WAF, Vercel
findings.description: Web Application Firewall or CDN detected: Cloudflare WAF, Vercel. This may filter malicious requests and provide DDoS protection.
findings.impact: WAF presence indicates an additional security layer, but may provide false sense of security if misconfigured
findings.remediation: Ensure WAF rules are properly configured. Regularly update WAF signatures.

findings.title: No Content-Security-Policy header on Main Application
findings.description: No Content-Security-Policy header is set. CSP is the primary defense against Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks and other injection-based attacks.
findings.evidence:
URL: https://app.archscale.in
Content-Security-Policy: (not set)
Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only: (not set)
findings.impact: Without CSP, the application has no browser-enforced protection against XSS, clickjacking via frames, or other injection attacks
findings.remediation:
Implement a strict Content-Security-Policy. Start with:
Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; font-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'self'; form-action 'self'; base-uri 'self'; object-src 'none'

findings.title: returnTo parameter appears to validate redirect targets
findings.description: Testing of the returnTo parameter with various bypass payloads did not result in successful open redirects. The server appears to validate redirect targets.
findings.evidence: Tested 23 payloads against https://auth.archscale.in/login?returnTo=<payload>. No external redirects observed.
findings.impact: Low — the redirect validation appears to be functioning correctly
findings.remediation: Continue monitoring. Ensure the allowlist is maintained as new subdomains are added.

findings.title: Error handling appears properly configured
findings.description: No information leakage was detected in error responses across all tested payloads and methods.
findings.evidence: Tested 24 error payloads, 6 HTTP methods, and multiple malformed request types
findings.impact: Positive — error pages do not leak sensitive internal details
findings.remediation: Continue monitoring. Ensure custom error handlers remain in place after updates.

findings.title: No rate limiting detected on Login Page
findings.description: No rate limiting was detected after sending 15 rapid requests to Login Page. All requests returned successful status codes without any throttling, CAPTCHA, or lockout.
findings.evidence:
URL: https://auth.archscale.in/login
Requests sent: 15
Status codes: [200, 200, 200, 200, 200, 200, 200, 200, 200, 200, 200, 200, 200, 200, 200]
Avg response time: 0.916s
Time increase factor: 1.1x
findings.impact: Without rate limiting, attackers can perform brute-force attacks against authentication, credential stuffing, or resource exhaustion attacks
findings.remediation:
Implement rate limiting on all authentication endpoints:
• Return 429 Too Many Requests after threshold
• Include Retry-After header
• Implement progressive delays
• Consider CAPTCHA after N failed attempts
• Implement IP-based and account-based rate limits
